title: Q1 plan for Dedicated Capacity ops, autoscale SLOs, and OKR alignment
creator: Marcus Liu
description:
Objective: Deliver a sprintable Q1 plan that operationalizes Dedicated Capacity SLAs, defines autoscale policies (predictable baseline + burst), and ties work to measurable OKRs. This ticket owns the cross-functional coordination, acceptance criteria, and runbook artifacts needed for launch-ready Dedicated autoscale controls and the customer migration playbook.

Why now: Enterprise deals in the pipeline expect clearer burst behavior and deterministic latency under mixed traffic. Current Dedicated deployments are brittle when customer workloads spike or when model variants are swapped. The target is to reduce P95 latency variance by 25% for committed capacity customers while keeping per-token unit cost within 10% of baseline through smarter autoscale and caching policies.

Scope (in-scope):
- Define autoscale policy primitives (min-reserved, burst-queue, prewarm windows, emergency fallback).
- Ops runbook for capacity incidents and automated remediation (traffic re-routing, temporary rate-limits, forced model-fallback).
- Canary experiment plan for autoscale policy A/B test across 10 pilot customers.
- Billing alignment: mapping reserved CPU/GPU tiers to pricing and crediting rules for burst consumption.
- Console UI endpoints: per-route autoscale toggle and visibility into reserved vs burst usage.
- SLO definition and alerting thresholds for Dedicated (latency P50/P95, queue depth, error rate).

Out-of-scope: Private on-prem packaging changes, deep kernel/runtime refactors beyond necessary autoscale hooks, and pricing contract negotiation for enterprise legal teams (we will supply playbook notes but not close deals).

Stakeholders: PM (Rhea Patel), Infra Eng (owner: Priya Rao), Serving Runtime (owner: Daniel Ortiz), Sales Engineering (owner: Lina Gomez), Billing (owner: Omar Khan), Support/Success (owner: Naomi White).

Success metrics (OKRs mapping):
- OKR: Increase reliability of Dedicated by Q1 end. KR1: P95 latency variance down 25% for committed customers (metric: per-route p95 over last 7d).
- OKR: Make burst predictable and economical. KR2: Average burst cost delta <= 10% of committed per-token baseline for pilot customers.
- OKR: Reduce operational toil. KR3: Time-to-resolve capacity incidents reduced from 3.6 hours to <60 minutes for incidents tied to autoscale behavior.

Deliverables & milestones (high-level):
- 2025-01-22: Finalize autoscale policy primitives and API spec (deliverable: autoscale-spec.md).
- 2025-02-05: Proto runbook + on-call playbook draft (deliverable: ops-runbook-v0).
- 2025-02-18: Canary experiment ready; pilot customers signed and onboarding guide published.
- 2025-03-10: Console UI for per-route controls in beta; pilot rollouts begin.
- 2025-03-28: Post-canary analysis and decision: promote policy, iterate, or rollback.

Trade-offs and decisions to surface: 
- Latency vs cost: More aggressive prewarm reduces latency but increases idle GPU minutes. Decision: prioritize latency for P1 committed customers, provide a toggle in UI to relax prewarm for lower-tier contracts.
- Predictability vs utilization: Keeping headroom improves SLA compliance but lowers overall utilization. We'll define two policy classes: "Committed-Strict" (higher headroom, tighter SLOs) and "Committed-CostOptimized" (lower headroom with better average utilization); customers can select at purchase.
- Complexity vs observability: Introducing many policy knobs increases operational complexity. Decision: start with a small orthogonal set (min-reserved, burst-cap, prewarm-window) and opaque, higher-level presets in the UI.

Acceptance criteria:
- Autoscale API spec merged in repo and documented in Confluence (link in links).
- Ops runbook covers 3 failure modes and includes escalation matrix and automated remediations.
- Canary launched with at least 10 pilot customers and automated telemetry collection (console dashboard shows reserved vs burst token breakdown).
- Billing mapping validated with Billing team; invoice simulation for pilot customers performed.
- Console UI provides toggle and a per-route breakdown; audit logs emitted for toggles.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Burst consumption causes outsized cost for Redwood when customers misconfigure. Mitigation: Soft limits and quota warnings; require Sales Engineering sign-off for high-burst tiers.
- Risk: Runtime incompatibilities with some model variants during autoscale. Mitigation: Maintain an automated compatibility matrix and fallback to verified model variants during burst.
- Risk: Delayed customer adoption due to contract complexity. Mitigation: build a one-click migration playbook and offer pilot discounts.

Notes & links: 
- Design spec: https://drive.redwood.com/design/dedicated-autoscale-v1 (draft)
- Autoscale API proto: https://github.com/redwood-inference/dedicated-autoscale/pulls/67
- Ops runbook draft: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/OPS/Dedicated+Autoscale+Runbook+v0
- Pilot sign-up sheet: https://forms.gle/pilot-signup-2025

Review requests & open questions for next sync: 
1) Sales: define how burst credits appear on invoices for committed vs uncommitted customers (owner: Omar).
2) Runtime: confirm fallback performance for model variants when KV-cache cannot be hot-warmed (owner: Daniel).
3) Console: scope for audit log retention and export (owner: Priya).

Next steps (short term):
- 2025-02-21: Bring the autoscale spec to PM+Infra+Runtime review (meeting invite sent).
- 2025-02-24: Finalize pilot customer list and onboarding checklist.
- 2025-03-03: Run first end-to-end smoke test with synthetic spike traffic.

Document owner & follow-up: This ticket will be the single source of truth for Q1 deliverables and will be updated with weekly status notes and links to PRs and dashboards.

comments: Priya Rao (Infra): We need a clear signal for when to prewarm GPUs for a predicted traffic surge. Proposing a short-lived prediction window based on 5-minute moving average.
Daniel Ortiz (Runtime): Fallback to quantized variant increases latency by ~30ms in our bench; acceptable for emergency fallback. Adding acceptance test for this.
Lina Gomez (Sales Eng): Pilot customers want clear dashboards that explain chargeback; add an item to the billing mapping to provide per-customer simulation exports.
